All these men had risen to the ranks of kings and princes, generals or primeministers. Their names were known even in neighboring states. Nonetheless,as soon as they were implicated in crimes and they fell into the net of the laws,not one of them was able to decide to commit suicide. When a person is sur-rounded by mire and filth, it has always been the same, in ancient and moderntimes: How can anyone not but be disgraced? Speaking from this point of view,courage or cowardice is a matter of the momentum of events, while strengthor weakness depends on the specific situation.48

This is probably why the Ancients took the application of themutilating punishments to high officials so seriously.

My draft was not yet finished when I met with this disaster. Thinking thatit would be a pity were my work not to be completed, I submitted to the mostextreme punishment without betraying any signs of resentment. If truly I canfinish this book and see it stored away in Famous Mountain,57 and then passeddown to the appropriate people, who will make it known in towns and bigcities, then I will have made up for the burden of my previous disgrace. Then,even if I were to suffer ten thousand deaths, how could I feel any regret? Thisbeing the case with me, this is something that can be discussed with wise men,but it is hard to speak of such things with vulgar people.

I met with this disaster as a resultof my words and I have become the butt of ridicule in my own hometown. Ihave disgraced my forebears. How could I ever again brazenly ascend the gravemounds of my parents?59 Even after one hundred generations the defilementwill only deepen! That is why my guts churn all day long.60 At home I am in adaze, as if I have lost something. Going out of the house, I forget where it is Iam going. Every time I think of this shame, my back breaks out in a sweat thatsoaks my robe. I am only an official serving in the women’s quarters.61 If onlyI could withdraw into deep seclusion among the crags and caves! For the timebeing, I must drift about, following the ordinary customs, going up and downwith the times, in order to get along with its reckless delusions.62
